```{=html}
<p>This page covers <b>views</b>, <b>transactions</b>, <b>integrity constraints</b>, <b>SQL data types</b> and <b>authorization</b>. Examples run on the course datasets; statements that change data are wrapped in <code>begin; … rollback;</code> so your copy of the dataset is left unchanged.</p>
<div class="flow tight"><div class="box"><b>Views</b><span>virtual relations</span></div><div class="box"><b>Transactions</b><span>all or nothing</span></div><div class="box"><b>Constraints</b><span>keep data valid</span></div><div class="box"><b>Data types</b><span>dates, domains, indexes</span></div><div class="box"><b>Authorization</b><span>who can do what</span></div></div>
```

## Views

### Why Views?

```{=html}
<p>Not every user should see every column. A clerk may need an instructor's id, name and department, but <b>not</b> the salary. A <b>view</b> is a named query that behaves like a "virtual relation": it stores no data of its own, and its query is substituted in wherever the view is used.</p>
<div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>instructor</b></div><span>id, name, dept_name, salary</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>view faculty</b></div><span>select id, name, dept_name</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>user query</b></div><span>sees only 3 columns</span></div></div>
```

### Creating and Using a View

```sql
create view v as <query expression>;
```

```{=html}
<div class="ds">Dataset: university</div>
```

```sql
create view faculty as
select id, name, dept_name
from instructor;

select * from faculty where dept_name = 'Biology';
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>id</th><th>name</th><th>dept_name</th></tr><tr><td>80759</td><td>Queiroz</td><td>Biology</td></tr><tr><td>81991</td><td>Valtchev</td><td>Biology</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(2 rows)</div><p>Salary is not visible through the view. Remove it afterwards with <code>drop view faculty;</code>.</p>
<p>A view can rename its columns and contain aggregates:</p>
```

```sql
create view departments_total_salary(dept_name, total_salary) as
select dept_name, sum(salary)
from instructor
group by dept_name;

select * from departments_total_salary
order by total_salary desc;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>dept_name</th><th>total_salary</th></tr><tr><td>Statistics</td><td>406772.65</td></tr><tr><td>Athletics</td><td>385490.99</td></tr><tr><td>Cybernetics</td><td>385386.27</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">First 3 of 17 rows shown</div>
```

### Views Defined Using Other Views

```sql
create view physics_fall_2006 as
select course.course_id, sec_id, building, room_number
from course, section
where course.course_id = section.course_id
      and course.dept_name = 'Physics'
      and section.semester = 'Fall' and section.year = 2006;

select * from physics_fall_2006;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>course_id</th><th>sec_id</th><th>building</th><th>room_number</th></tr><tr><td>376</td><td>1</td><td>Power</td><td>717</td></tr><tr><td>959</td><td>1</td><td>Saucon</td><td>180</td></tr><tr><td>239</td><td>1</td><td>Taylor</td><td>183</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(3 rows) · row order may vary</div>
```

```sql
create view physics_fall_2006_taylor as
select course_id, room_number
from physics_fall_2006
where building = 'Taylor';

select * from physics_fall_2006_taylor;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>course_id</th><th>room_number</th></tr><tr><td>239</td><td>183</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(1 row)</div>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt "><tr><th>Term</th><th>Meaning</th></tr><tr><td>v1 <b>depends directly on</b> v2</td><td>v2 is used in the definition of v1 (physics_fall_2006_taylor → physics_fall_2006)</td></tr><tr><td>v1 <b>depends on</b> v2</td><td>there is a chain of direct dependencies from v1 to v2</td></tr><tr><td><b>recursive</b> view</td><td>a view that depends on itself</td></tr></table></div>
```

### View Expansion

```{=html}
<p>To evaluate a query on a view, the system repeatedly replaces each view name with its defining query until only base relations remain. This terminates as long as no view is recursive.</p>
<div class="panel"><div class="panel-title">Expanding select * from physics_fall_2006_taylor</div><div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>step 0</b></div><span>from physics_fall_2006_taylor</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>step 1</b></div><span>replace it: from physics_fall_2006 where building = 'Taylor'</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>step 2</b></div><span>replace physics_fall_2006 with its course ⋈ section query</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>done</b></div><span>only base relations left</span></div></div></div>
```

```sql
-- fully expanded query
select course_id, room_number
from (select course.course_id, sec_id, building, room_number
      from course, section
      where course.course_id = section.course_id
            and course.dept_name = 'Physics'
            and section.semester = 'Fall' and section.year = 2006) as physics_fall_2006
where building = 'Taylor';
```

### Updating Through Views

```{=html}
<p>An insert into a view must be translated into an insert into the base relation. Columns not in the view become <code>null</code>.</p>
```

```sql
begin;
create view faculty as select id, name, dept_name from instructor;
insert into faculty values ('30765', 'Green', 'Biology');
select * from instructor where id = '30765';
rollback;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>id</th><th>name</th><th>dept_name</th><th>salary</th></tr><tr><td>30765</td><td>Green</td><td>Biology</td><td><span class="nl">null</span></td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(1 row)</div>
<div class="panel"><div class="panel-title">What PostgreSQL does with different view inserts</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt "><tr><th>View</th><th>Insert</th><th>Result</th></tr><tr class="hit"><td>faculty (one table, plain columns)</td><td>('30765','Green','Biology')</td><td>✓ inserted, salary = <span class="nl">null</span></td></tr><tr><td>faculty</td><td>('30765','Green','Music')</td><td>✗ foreign key error: no department Music</td></tr><tr class="hit"><td>biology_faculty: <code>… where dept_name = 'Biology'</code></td><td>('30766','Brown','Physics')</td><td>✓ inserted, but <b>not visible</b> through the view</td></tr><tr><td>same view <code>with check option</code></td><td>('30766','Brown','Physics')</td><td>✗ new row violates check option</td></tr><tr><td>departments_total_salary (group by)</td><td>('Music', 100000)</td><td>✗ views containing group by are not updatable</td></tr><tr><td>instructor_info (instructor ⋈ department)</td><td>('69987','White','Taylor')</td><td>✗ views on more than one table are not updatable</td></tr></table></div></div>
```

```sql
begin;
create view biology_faculty as
select id, name, dept_name from instructor
where dept_name = 'Biology';

insert into biology_faculty values ('30766', 'Brown', 'Physics');
select * from biology_faculty;      -- Brown is not here
rollback;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>id</th><th>name</th><th>dept_name</th></tr><tr><td>80759</td><td>Queiroz</td><td>Biology</td></tr><tr><td>81991</td><td>Valtchev</td><td>Biology</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(2 rows) · the row was inserted into instructor, but it fails the view's where clause</div>
```

```sql
-- add with check option to reject such rows
create view biology_faculty as
select id, name, dept_name from instructor
where dept_name = 'Biology'
with check option;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><pre>ERROR:  new row violates check option for view "biology_faculty"
DETAIL:  Failing row contains (30766, Brown, Physics, null).</pre>
<p>A view is updatable (in SQL and PostgreSQL) only if: the <code>from</code> clause has <b>one</b> relation; the <code>select</code> has only plain column names (no expressions, aggregates or <code>distinct</code>); columns left out can be <code>null</code>; and there is no <code>group by</code> or <code>having</code>.</p>
```

### Materialized Views

```{=html}
<p>A <b>materialized view</b> stores the query result physically. Reading it is fast, but it does not change when the base relations change until it is <b>refreshed</b>.</p><div class="ds">Dataset: university</div>
```

```sql
begin;
create materialized view dept_count as
select dept_name, count(*) as num_instructors
from instructor group by dept_name;

select * from dept_count where dept_name = 'Biology';     -- 2
insert into instructor values ('30765', 'Green', 'Biology', 72000);
select * from dept_count where dept_name = 'Biology';     -- still 2
refresh materialized view dept_count;
select * from dept_count where dept_name = 'Biology';     -- 3
rollback;
```

```{=html}
<div class="panel"><div class="panel-title">num_instructors for Biology</div><div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>create</b></div><span>view stores 2</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>insert into instructor</b></div><span>base has 3, view still shows 2 (stale)</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>refresh</b></div><span>view shows 3</span></div></div></div>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt "><tr><th></th><th>View</th><th>Materialized view</th></tr><tr><td>Stores data</td><td>No, only the query</td><td>Yes, the result</td></tr><tr><td>Read speed</td><td>Recomputed on every use</td><td>Fast</td></tr><tr><td>Up to date</td><td>Always</td><td>Only after refresh</td></tr></table></div>
<p>⚠️ A relation cannot be dropped while a view depends on it:</p>
```

```sql
drop table instructor;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><pre>ERROR:  cannot drop table instructor because other objects depend on it
DETAIL:  constraint advisor_i_id_fkey on table advisor depends on table instructor
constraint teaches_id_fkey on table teaches depends on table instructor
view faculty depends on table instructor
HINT:  Use DROP ... CASCADE to drop the dependent objects too.</pre>
```

## Transactions

```{=html}
<p>A <b>transaction</b> is a unit of work: a sequence of statements that must succeed or fail <b>as a whole</b>.</p>
<div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>begin</b></div><span>start the unit of work</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>statements</b></div><span>queries and updates</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>commit work</b></div><span>make all changes permanent</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>or rollback work</b></div><span>undo everything since begin</span></div></div>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt "><tr><th>Property</th><th>Meaning</th></tr><tr><td>Atomic</td><td>either every statement takes effect, or none does</td></tr><tr><td>Isolated</td><td>a transaction does not see the half-finished changes of others running at the same time</td></tr></table></div>
<p>The SQL standard starts a transaction implicitly. PostgreSQL runs in <b>autocommit</b> mode: each statement is its own transaction unless you write <code>begin</code>.</p>
<p><i>Example:</i> give Physics a 10% raise and add a new instructor in one transaction.</p><div class="ds">Dataset: university</div>
```

```sql
begin;
update instructor set salary = salary * 1.10 where dept_name = 'Physics';
insert into instructor values ('99999', 'Test', 'Physics', 20000);
select count(*) from instructor;
commit;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><pre>UPDATE 2
ERROR:  new row for relation "instructor" violates check constraint "instructor_salary_check"
ERROR:  current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block
ROLLBACK</pre>
<div class="panel"><div class="panel-title">What happened</div><div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>update</b></div><span>2 rows changed</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>insert</b></div><span>fails: salary must be &gt; 29000</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>select</b></div><span>ignored: transaction aborted</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>commit</b></div><span>becomes ROLLBACK</span></div></div><p style="margin:6px 0 0">The raise is undone too: Physics salaries are still 108011.81 and 121141.99. One failed statement aborts the whole transaction.</p></div>
```

## Integrity Constraints

```{=html}
<p>Constraints stop changes that would make the data inconsistent. They are checked on every insert and update.</p>
```

### Constraints on a Single Relation

```{=html}
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt "><tr><th>Constraint</th><th>Meaning</th></tr><tr><td><code>not null</code></td><td>the column cannot be null</td></tr><tr><td><code>primary key (A1, …)</code></td><td>unique and not null; identifies each row</td></tr><tr><td><code>unique (A1, …)</code></td><td>a candidate key; unlike a primary key, its columns may be null</td></tr><tr><td><code>check (P)</code></td><td>every row must satisfy predicate P</td></tr></table></div>
<p>The university dataset is created with these constraints (from <code>university.sql</code>):</p>
```

```sql
create table instructor (
    id        varchar(5),
    name      varchar(20) not null,
    dept_name varchar(20),
    salary    numeric(8,2) check (salary > 29000),
    primary key (id),
    foreign key (dept_name) references department
        on delete set null
);

create table section (
    ...
    semester varchar(6)
        check (semester in ('Fall', 'Winter', 'Spring', 'Summer')),
    year numeric(4,0) check (year > 1701 and year < 2100),
    ...
);
```

```{=html}
<div class="panel"><div class="panel-title">Try to break them</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt "><tr><th>Statement</th><th>Error</th></tr><tr><td>insert into instructor values ('63395', 'Copy', 'Biology', 50000);</td><td>duplicate key value violates unique constraint "instructor_pkey"</td></tr><tr><td>insert into instructor values ('30767', null, 'Biology', 50000);</td><td>null value in column "name" … violates not-null constraint</td></tr><tr><td>insert into instructor values ('99999', 'Test', 'Physics', 20000);</td><td>violates check constraint "instructor_salary_check"</td></tr><tr><td>insert into course values ('CS-997', 'Test', 'Comp. Sci.', 0);</td><td>violates check constraint "course_credits_check"</td></tr><tr><td>insert into section values ('105', '9', 'Autumn', 2009, null, null, null);</td><td>violates check constraint "section_semester_check"</td></tr><tr><td>insert into instructor values ('30768', 'Lee', 'Music', 50000);</td><td>violates foreign key constraint "instructor_dept_name_fkey"</td></tr></table></div></div>
<p>⚠️ A <code>check</code> constraint passes when its predicate is <b>unknown</b>. <code>salary &gt; 29000</code> with a <code>null</code> salary is unknown, so a null salary is allowed (that is why the view insert above worked).</p>
```

### Referential Integrity

```{=html}
<p>A value that appears in one relation for a given set of attributes must also appear in another relation. If <code>A</code> is the primary key of <code>S</code>, then <code>A</code> is a <b>foreign key</b> in <code>R</code> if every value of <code>A</code> in <code>R</code> also appears in <code>S</code>.</p>
```

#### Cascading actions

```{=html}
<p>What happens to referencing rows when the referenced row is deleted or updated:</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt "><tr><th>Action</th><th>Effect</th><th>In the university dataset</th></tr><tr><td><code>cascade</code></td><td>delete / update the referencing rows too</td><td>takes.id → student, advisor.s_id → student</td></tr><tr><td><code>set null</code></td><td>set the foreign key to null</td><td>instructor.dept_name → department</td></tr><tr><td><code>set default</code></td><td>set the foreign key to its default value</td><td>not used</td></tr><tr><td><code>no action</code> (default)</td><td>reject the delete / update</td><td>prereq.prereq_id → course</td></tr></table></div>
<div class="panel"><div class="panel-title">The three behaviours on real data (all inside begin … rollback)</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt "><tr><th>Statement</th><th>What happens</th></tr><tr><td>delete from student where id = '1000';</td><td>✓ deleted; <b>cascade</b> also removes their 13 <code>takes</code> rows and 1 <code>advisor</code> row</td></tr><tr><td>delete from department where dept_name = 'Biology';</td><td>✓ deleted; <b>set null</b>: Queiroz and Valtchev now have dept_name = <span class="nl">null</span></td></tr><tr><td>delete from course where course_id = '130';</td><td>✗ <b>no action</b>: Key (course_id)=(130) is still referenced from table "prereq"</td></tr></table></div></div>
```

#### The chicken-and-egg problem

```{=html}
<p>If two relations reference each other (for example a person and their spouse), or a relation references itself, the first row cannot be inserted while the constraint is checked immediately. Options: insert one side with <code>null</code> first and update it later (not possible if the column is <code>not null</code>), or <b>defer</b> constraint checking to the end of the transaction:</p>
```

```sql
create table person (
    id char(10) primary key,
    name char(40),
    spouse char(10),
    foreign key (spouse) references person
        deferrable initially deferred
);

begin;
insert into person values ('P1', 'Asha', 'P2');   -- P2 does not exist yet: allowed
insert into person values ('P2', 'Ravi', 'P1');
commit;                                          -- checked here: both exist
```

## SQL Data Types and Schemas

### Date and time types

```{=html}
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt "><tr><th>Type</th><th>Stores</th><th>Example</th></tr><tr><td><code>date</code></td><td>year, month, day</td><td>date '2020-05-06'</td></tr><tr><td><code>time</code></td><td>hour, minute, second</td><td>time '09:00:30'</td></tr><tr><td><code>timestamp</code></td><td>date and time</td><td>timestamp '2020-05-06 09:00:30.75'</td></tr><tr><td><code>interval</code></td><td>a period of time</td><td>interval '7 days'</td></tr></table></div><p>Subtracting two dates gives a difference; adding an interval to a date gives a new date and time.</p><div class="ds">Dataset: flis</div>
```

```sql
select date '2020-05-09' - date '2020-05-06' as days_between;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>days_between</th></tr><tr><td>3</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(1 row)</div>
```

```sql
select match_num, match_date, match_date + interval '7 days' as rematch
from matches
order by match_num;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>match_num</th><th>match_date</th><th>rematch</th></tr><tr><td>M0001</td><td>2020-05-06</td><td>2020-05-13 00:00:00</td></tr><tr><td>M0002</td><td>2020-05-07</td><td>2020-05-14 00:00:00</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">First 2 of 16 rows shown · date + interval returns a timestamp</div>
```

```sql
select name, dob, extract(year from dob) as birth_year
from players
order by player_id;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>name</th><th>dob</th><th>birth_year</th></tr><tr><td>Rudra</td><td>2003-05-01</td><td>2003</td></tr><tr><td>Advik</td><td>2004-06-01</td><td>2004</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">First 2 of 71 rows shown</div>
```

### Index creation

```{=html}
<p>An index lets the system find rows with a given value without scanning the whole relation. Primary keys get an index automatically.</p>
```

```sql
create index match_date_index on matches(match_date);

-- this lookup can now use the index
select * from matches where match_date = '2020-05-06';
```

### User-defined types and domains

```{=html}
<p>The SQL standard has <code>create type</code> (like a typedef) and <code>create domain</code> (a type that can also carry constraints).</p>
```

```sql
-- SQL standard
create type dollars as numeric(12,2) final;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><pre>ERROR:  syntax error at or near "numeric"</pre><p>PostgreSQL does not support this form of <code>create type</code>; use a <b>domain</b> instead:</p><div class="ds">Dataset: flis</div>
```

```sql
begin;
create domain dollars as numeric(12,2) check (value >= 0);
create table prize (team_id varchar(5), amount dollars);
insert into prize values ('T0001', 5000);   -- ok
insert into prize values ('T0002', -10);    -- fails
rollback;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><pre>INSERT 0 1
ERROR:  value for domain dollars violates check constraint "dollars_check"</pre>
```

### Large-object types

```{=html}
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt "><tr><th>Standard SQL</th><th>Stores</th><th>PostgreSQL equivalent</th></tr><tr><td><code>blob</code></td><td>binary large object (images, video)</td><td><code>bytea</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>clob</code></td><td>character large object (documents)</td><td><code>text</code></td></tr></table></div><p>When a query returns a large object, the system returns a pointer (locator) to it rather than the object itself.</p>
```

## Authorization

```{=html}
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt "><tr><th>On data</th><th>On schema</th></tr><tr><td><code>select</code> (read)</td><td><code>index</code>: create and drop indexes</td></tr><tr><td><code>insert</code></td><td><code>resources</code>: create new relations</td></tr><tr><td><code>update</code></td><td><code>alteration</code>: add or drop attributes</td></tr><tr><td><code>delete</code></td><td><code>drop</code>: delete relations</td></tr></table></div>
```

### Granting and revoking

```sql
grant <privilege list> on <relation or view> to <user list>;
revoke <privilege list> on <relation or view> from <user list>;
```

```{=html}
<p>The user list can be a user, a role, or <code>public</code>. The grantor must hold the privilege (or be the database administrator).</p>
```

### Roles

```{=html}
<p>A role groups privileges. Granting a role to a user (or to another role) passes on all of its privileges.</p><div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>create role ta</b></div><span>grant select on instructor to ta</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>grant ta to amit</b></div><span>amit inherits select</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>set role amit</b></div><span>test what amit can do</span></div></div><div class="ds">Dataset: university</div>
```

```sql
create role ta;
create role amit;
grant select on instructor to ta;
grant ta to amit;

set role amit;
select count(*) from instructor;                                -- allowed
update instructor set salary = salary where id = '80759';      -- not granted
select count(*) from student;                                   -- not granted
reset role;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><pre> count
-------
    50

ERROR:  permission denied for table instructor
ERROR:  permission denied for table student</pre>
```

### Authorization on views

```{=html}
<p>A user can be given access to a view <b>without</b> access to the relation underneath, which is how views hide data.</p>
```

```sql
create view biology_faculty as
select id, name, dept_name from instructor where dept_name = 'Biology';
create role bio_staff;
grant select on biology_faculty to bio_staff;

set role bio_staff;
select * from biology_faculty;          -- works
select count(*) from instructor;        -- denied
reset role;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><pre>  id   |   name   | dept_name
-------+----------+-----------
 80759 | Queiroz  | Biology
 81991 | Valtchev | Biology

ERROR:  permission denied for table instructor</pre>
```

### Passing privileges on, and revoking them

```{=html}
<p><code>with grant option</code> lets the receiver grant the privilege further. Revoking it then has to deal with the privileges that depend on it.</p><div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>dba → amit</b></div><span>select with grant option</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>amit → satoshi</b></div><span>select</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>revoke from amit</b></div><span>restrict: error · cascade: satoshi loses it too</span></div></div>
```

```sql
create role satoshi;
grant select on department to amit with grant option;
set role amit;
grant select on department to satoshi;
reset role;

revoke select on department from amit restrict;
revoke select on department from amit cascade;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><pre>ERROR:  dependent privileges exist
HINT:  Use CASCADE to revoke them too.
REVOKE</pre>
<p>After the cascade, <code>satoshi</code> gets <code>permission denied for table department</code>. In PostgreSQL the default for <code>revoke</code> is <code>restrict</code>.</p><p>The <code>references</code> privilege is needed to declare a foreign key to someone else's relation, because a foreign key restricts what the owner of the referenced relation can delete or update: <code>grant references (dept_name) on department to mariano;</code></p><p>Clean up afterwards with <code>drop view</code> and <code>drop role</code> for everything created in this section.</p>
```
